description: RPX Optimization has commenced a new engagement titled "Transformation at ACCHCO" with Alexandria Container & Cargo Handling Co (ACCHCO), the operator of the main container terminal at the Port of Alexandria. The project involves a full operational transformation covering yard restructuring, berth scheduling, and equipment deployment, with Felix leading the modeling work.

timeline.entry: RPX Optimization's Managing Director Michael Dempsey announced that the firm will pursue a full operational transformation for Alexandria Container & Cargo Handling Co, assigning Felix to lead the modeling work and naming the engagement "Transformation at ACCHCO".

RPX Optimization’s Managing Director Michael Dempsey informed Felix that the firm will lead the modeling for a full operational transformation—including yard restructuring, berth scheduling, and equipment deployment—at Alexandria Container & Cargo Handling Co, to be called “Transformation at ACCHCO.”

RPX Optimization Managing Director Felix Kasiske confirmed he will lead the modeling, reviewed the ACCHCO RFP highlighting an aging straddle‑carrier fleet and severe peak‑season yard congestion, and proposed a three‑phase project plan (diagnostics, redesign, implementation support).

RPX Optimization's Managing Director Felix Kasiske agreed to lead the modeling for ACCHCO's project, identified the main constraints as an aging straddle-carrier fleet and severe peak-season yard congestion, and proposed a three-phase approach of diagnostics, redesign, and implementation support.

RPX Optimization kicked off Phase 1 diagnostics for ACCHCO in Alexandria, secured full access to the terminal operating system data, and identified a yard utilization peak of 94%, well above the 75% best‑practice threshold.

RPX Optimization kicked off Phase 1 diagnostics for ACCHCO in Alexandria, gained full access to the terminal operating system data, identified yard utilization peaking at 94% (above the 75% best‑practice threshold), and began building a simulation model.

RPX Optimization GmbH’s Managing Director Felix Kasiske reported that Phase 1 of their yard‑congestion simulation was completed, identified poor block allocation—not lack of space—as the cause, projected a roughly 20 % capacity gain through re‑zoning, and announced moving into Phase 2 redesign with a two‑day operations‑team workshop scheduled for early May.

RPX Optimization announced that Phase 1 of its simulation study was complete, identifying poor block allocation as the cause of yard congestion and projecting a roughly 20% capacity gain from re‑zoning, and scheduled two days with the operations team in early May to begin Phase 2 redesign.
RPX Optimization states it has completed over 225 projects worldwide and lists its leadership as Managing Director Dr. Felix Kasiske (Germany) and VP Business Development Michael Dempsey (USA).
